doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Wrapping up and Monk Rowe describes the Hamilton archive
summary: Closing thoughts, and Rowe describes the college, its archive begun in 1995 with 400+ interviews, and his job.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: All right. Well that sounds like a good note to wrap up with. And I’ve so much enjoyed this conversation. I had a feeling I would.
But did you get enough information?
I did. We might have to do part two down the road.

That’s fine, and I’ve got more stories for you if you need — I just really appreciate you thinking of me, and Denis thinking of me. So it’s always an honor to talk about my — this helps keep his legacy alive. And that’s the thing that’s very — tell me about your school and tell me about your archives if you can.
Well Hamilton College is a very old college. It goes back to the early 1800s. It’s a liberal arts school. It’s small. It’s a gorgeous place, a nice place to work.
How many music students do they have?

We don’t have many music majors. We have a nice crop of talented students, we have about six professors. This project I do came about because a Hamilton grad of the class of 1944 was a very enthusiastic supporter of swing music and, you know, jazz of the 30s through the 50s. And he decided that many of his musical heroes were passing away without having their stories told. So I lucked into the job of starting to do videotaped interviews and we decided together, you know we focused on people with the Basie orchestra first. Because Joe Williams the singer helped us get started.
Yeah. So we’ve been at it since 1995 and we’ve done 400 plus video interviews. It’s been a dream gig for me I’ll tell you that.
Oh you can’t beat that man. You can’t beat getting paid for doing this.
Wait a minute you mean I could get paid for this?
I teach saxophone lessons and an ensemble. And the archive job is a half-time job at the college so I’m there like 65%.
Yeah. And it gives me time to play gigs, not right now.
